details.response_text:
Step 1. Analyze the question and identify the relevant metrics:
The relevant metrics for monitoring the pods of the ticket cancellation service to determine if any pods were restarted in the past hour and now have memory usage greater than 8GB, while excluding pods whose memory usage is less than 60% of the requested limit resource are:
- The metric "kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total" indicates the number of container restarts per container. This metric can be used to identify pods that were restarted.
- The metric "container_memory_usage_bytes" represents the current memory usage in bytes, which can be used to check if the memory usage is greater than 8GB.
- The metric "container_memory_max_usage_bytes" denotes the maximum memory usage recorded in bytes, which can be compared to the memory limit to exclude pods with memory usage less than 60% of the limit.
Step 2. Relevant Metrics List:
```
- {"name": "kube_pod_container_status_restarts_total", "type": "counter", "description": "[STABLE] The number of container restarts per container."}
- {"name": "container_memory_usage_bytes", "type": "gauge", "description": "Current memory usage in bytes, including all memory regardless of when it was accessed"}
- {"name": "container_memory_max_usage_bytes", "type": "gauge", "description": "Maximum memory usage recorded in bytes"}
```

The relevant metrics for the filesystem usage and limit bytes for all containers of the auth service are:
- The metric "container_fs_usage_bytes" indicates the number of bytes currently consumed by the container on the filesystem. This measures the actual filesystem usage by the container.
- The metric "container_fs_limit_bytes" denotes the maximum number of bytes that can be consumed by the container on this filesystem. This represents the limit set for filesystem usage by the container.

```
